title: Protocol to quantify mechanical properties of cells using optical tweezers
author: Rodenburg, Eeftens

steps.title: Coat flow cell with fibronectin
steps.instruction: Prepare a 10 µg ml⁻¹ fibronectin solution in sterile 1× PBS, add ~110 µL to fully cover the flow‑cell channel, and incubate 2 h at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Dilute fibronectin to 10 µg ml⁻¹ in sterile 1× PBS.
Place the pipette tip directly in the channel; tilt the flow cell slightly to aid flow.
Add ~110 µL of the solution to cover the entire channel.
Incubate for 2 h at RT.

steps.title: Remove excess coating solution
steps.instruction: Flush the channel three times with growth medium, removing excess liquid from the opposite reservoir each time; avoid aspirating to prevent bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Fill one reservoir with growth medium (GM).
Tilt the flow cell and let liquid flow through the channel.
Remove excess liquid from the opposite reservoir.
Repeat the fill‑tilt‑remove cycle three times.
Remove any remaining liquid from both reservoirs (do not aspirate).

steps.title: Harvest and count adherent cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells in pre‑warmed GM, determine concentration with an automatic counter or hemocytometer, and ensure 60–80 % confluency; optional trypan‑blue viability check.

steps.title: Seed cells into flow cell
steps.instruction: Dilute 30 000 cells in 200 µL GM, then perform three exchange cycles of 60 µL between opposite reservoirs, removing excess liquid each time.

substeps.instruction: Dilute 30 000 cells in 200 µL GM.
Add 60 µL of the cell suspension to one reservoir.
Remove 60 µL from the opposite reservoir.
Repeat the add‑remove cycle three times.
Remove any excess liquid from the reservoirs.

steps.title: Verify cell dispersion
steps.instruction: Inspect the flow cell under a microscope to confirm that single cells are well dispersed.

steps.title: Incubate cells overnight
steps.instruction: Fill both reservoirs with GM, cap them, and incubate the flow cell at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ for 24 h.

steps.title: Remove excess medium
steps.instruction: Empty any surplus medium from the reservoirs before bead addition.

steps.title: Add beads to adherent cells
steps.instruction: Vortex bead stock, dilute 3 µL bead solution in 197 µL live‑cell medium (LCM), then perform three exchange cycles of 60 µL between opposite reservoirs; fill reservoirs with LCM and cap.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the bead solution.
Prepare bead‑LCM mix: 3 µL bead solution + 197 µL LCM.
Add 60 µL of the mix to one reservoir and remove 60 µL from the opposite reservoir.
Repeat the add‑remove cycle three times.
Fill both reservoirs with LCM.
Close the reservoirs with caps.

steps.title: Prepare flow cell for measurement
steps.instruction: The flow cell is now ready for optical‑tweezers measurements; handle gently to avoid cell detachment.

steps.title: Harvest and count suspended cells
steps.instruction: Harvest cells in pre‑warmed live‑cell medium (LCM), determine concentration, and confirm 60–80 % confluency; optional trypan‑blue viability check.

steps.title: Add beads and cell mixture
steps.instruction: Vortex bead stock, then dilute 3000 cells together with 3 µL bead solution in a total of 110 µL LCM; add the mixture directly into the flow‑cell channel to cover the area.

substeps.instruction: Vortex the bead solution.
Combine 3000 cells, 3 µL bead solution, and LCM to a final volume of 110 µL.
Place the pipette tip directly in the channel and tilt the flow cell slightly while adding to ensure even coverage.

steps.title: Verify suspended cell dispersion
steps.instruction: Examine the channel under a microscope to ensure single cells are well dispersed.

steps.title: Incubate to allow settling
steps.instruction: Fill the reservoirs with LCM, cap them, and incubate the flow cell for 30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ to let cells settle.

steps.title: Prepare suspended flow cell for measurement
steps.instruction: The flow cell is now ready for optical‑tweezers measurements on suspended cells.

steps.title: Load raw data into analysis software
steps.instruction: Open the .h5 files containing force and bead‑position data with Pylake (or equivalent) for further processing.

steps.title: Identify point of contact
steps.instruction: Define t₀ as the last data point before the force rises above 0 pN.

steps.title: Convert bead position to deformation
steps.instruction: Subtract the bead position at t₀ from the position at each subsequent time point to obtain deformation versus time.

steps.title: Determine target‑force time
steps.instruction: Find t_target, the time when the force first reaches 100 pN.

steps.title: Quantify deformation at tend
steps.instruction: Measure deformation at tend, defined as 10 s after t_target (or another user‑defined interval).

steps.title: Quantify creep under constant force
steps.instruction: Calculate the deformation change between t_target and tend while the force remains constant.

steps.title: Calculate spring constant
steps.instruction: Plot force versus deformation from t₀ onward, exclude data points within the first and last 10 pN, fit the linear elastic region, and take the slope as the spring constant k.

substeps.instruction: Generate a force‑deformation curve starting at t₀.
Discard points where force is <10 pN or > (maximum‑10 pN).
Perform linear regression on the remaining data.
Record the slope of the fit as k.
